sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: through this sum alone, compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 33% to about 4%, non-anginal chest pain to about 7% and atypical angina to about 11%, and being a woman lowers it to about 18%; chest pain type and sex also act through the sex and exercise angina part (below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 33% at 0 to about 94% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; more ST depression on exercise (from about 25% at 0 mm to about 61% at 2.8 mm), higher cholesterol (from about 21% at 193 mg/dL to about 56% at 308 mg/dL) and older age (from about 22% at 42 to about 43% at 66 years) raise it steadily.

Through this sum alone, a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 80%, a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 62% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 37%; the ST segment also acts through a small part, and the thallium scan and fasting blood sugar through the sex and exercise angina part (below).

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Some rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 2 to 17): through this sum alone a thallium result coded 4 raises the risk to about 94% and a downsloping ST segment to about 41%, and a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 22%; the model ignores resting blood pressure, maximum heart rate and the resting ECG.

This part combines sex, chest pain type, fasting blood sugar, chest pain on exercise and the thallium scan; through it, being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 33% to about 4%.
Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the risk more when exercise does not bring on chest pain: from about 33% to about 2%, against about 19% to about 9% when it does.
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL works the same way: it lowers the risk from about 33% to about 8% without chest pain on exercise, but takes it from about 19% to about 21% with it.
A reversible defect on the thallium scan raises the risk, and even more so if exercise brings on chest pain: from about 19% to about 43% then, against about 33% to about 34% when it does not.

This small part reads only the slope of the ST segment and barely changes the predictions: through it, an ST segment other than upsloping takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 33% to about 35%.

lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results) the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about 33%; it adds up most of its inputs independently, one part adds a combination of sex, chest pain on exercise and three other inputs to that sum, and a second part barely changes it.

evidence.text: Through it, being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 33% to about 4%, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 7%, and a reversible defect on the thallium scan to about 14%.

Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the risk from about 33% to about 2% when exercise does not bring on chest pain, against about 19% to about 9% when it does, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL from about 33% to about 8%, against about 19% to about 21%.
A reversible defect on the thallium scan raises the risk from about 19% to about 43% when exercise brings on chest pain, against about 33% to about 34% when it does not.
Atypical angina lowers it from about 19% to about 5% when exercise brings on chest pain, and from about 33% to about 11% when it does not.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part lowers the predicted risk for women and for patients with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL, mainly when exercise does not bring on chest pain, and makes a reversible defect on the thallium scan count mainly when exercise brings on chest pain.

evidence.text: Through it, an ST segment other than upsloping takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 33% to about 35%, and switching it off barely changes the predictions.
Its formula reproduces the part exactly on all 242 training patients.

hypothesis.text: This part passes on the slope of the ST segment and barely changes the predictions.

evidence.text: It is made up of the inputs that feed the score directly and two parts, the sex and exercise angina part and the upsloping ST segment offset (each explained below); the score is their sum, which was checked on all 242 training patients.
Chest pain on exercise does not feed the score directly, so it acts only through the sex and exercise angina part.

Changing one input at a time across the whole model, being a woman takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 33% to about 2%, against about 18% through the sum alone, and a flat rather than upsloping ST segment to about 81%.

Across the whole model, a reversible defect on the thallium scan takes it from about 33% to about 34%, against about 62% through the sum alone, because through the sex and exercise angina part it lowers the risk to about 14%.
The model ignores resting blood pressure, maximum heart rate and the resting ECG.

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the risk logit is additive: a logistic-regression core over 14 direct input edges (dominated by ca +1.57, cp:4 +1.30, slope:2 +1.04, oldpeak +0.66, chol +0.65, thal:7 +0.58; all risk-raising except thal:6 -0.13) plus two child terms: -0.760 h1213 + 0.384 g47 from sex_exang_interaction (the only route by which exercise angina affects risk, and only materially for women) and -0.065 x 3660 from slope1_offset (near-inert). The output node applies ReLU and the model then applies a sigmoid, so p = sigmoid(relu(z)): negative logits (60% of train) all map to p=0.5 and the decision is z>0. The 8 inputs cp:1, trestbps, restecg:0/1/2, thalach, exang:1 and thal:3 have no edges in the phenotype and are included as entries with zero effect. Evidence (train, n=242): full AUC 0.9457 / acc 0.876; linear core alone (children at their means) AUC 0.9255 / acc 0.855; logit SD 3.58 total, 3.42 linear core, 1.04 interaction block, 0.029 slope:1 term. Node-0 sensitivity ranks ca 0.63, cp:4 0.52, slope:2 0.42, oldpeak 0.27, chol 0.26, exang:0 0.26 (via the block).

parts.name: sex_exang_interaction
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: a sex x exercise-angina interaction built from two chained ReLU gates. Gate 1213 = relu(1.23 sex:0 + 1.31 exang:0 - 0.509 cp:2 - 0.563 fbs:0 + 0.476 thal:7 + 0.091) is a female-without-exercise-angina score; gate 47 = relu(1.43 + 0.956 exang:0 - 1.93 h1213) fires for patients without exercise angina whose 1213 score is low (mostly men) and is shut off by 1213. The output reads -0.760 h1213 + 0.384 g47. Evidence (train, n=242): group mean block logit is +0.04 (male, exang), +0.18 (male, no exang), -0.39 (female, exang), -1.76 (female, no exang). Exercise angina has no direct edge to the output, so its entire effect is this block: flipping exang no->yes raises the logit by +1.81 on average for women (range 0.78..2.11) but by -0.17 for men (range -0.78..1.87). g47 is active for 84% of men without angina but 19% of women without angina. cp:2, fbs:0 and thal:7 only shift h1213 (sensitivities 0.22-0.26 vs 0.57-0.60 for sex:0/exang:0). Odd signs (thal:7 and fbs:1 making the block slightly less protective / more protective respectively) are small modifiers we do not interpret clinically. Ablating gate 47 to its mean drops train AUC 0.9457->0.9414; ablating 1213->output drops it to 0.9347.

parts.name: slope1_offset
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: a near-inert affine pass-through of slope:1 (upsloping ST segment). Evidence: the ReLU pre-activation 0.446 slope:1 + 0.797 lies in [0.373, 1.266] on train, so it never clips; through the -0.0648 readout it adds -0.029 slope:1 - 0.052 to the logit (logit SD 0.029). Ablating it to its mean changes train AUC 0.9457->0.9454. It is a vestigial linear term, slightly protective for upsloping ST.

ann_28.text: The model gives a clearly higher predicted risk of heart disease if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect than if thallium stress test result is something other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan, and even more so if exercise brings on chest pain: for a typical patient, going from thallium stress test result other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan to a reversible defect on the thallium scan moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 19% to about 43% if exercise brings on chest pain, and from about 33% to about 34% if exercise does not bring on chest pain.

The model gives a clearly lower predicted risk of heart disease if fasting blood sugar is above 120 mg/dL than if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain: for a typical patient, going from fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less to fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 33% to about 8% if exercise does not bring on chest pain, and from about 19% to about 21% if exercise brings on chest pain.

The model gives a clearly lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient is a woman than if the patient is a man, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain: for a typical patient, going from male to female moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 33% to about 2% if exercise does not bring on chest pain, and from about 19% to about 9% if exercise brings on chest pain.

For a typical patient, going from chest pain type other than atypical angina to atypical angina moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 19% to about 5% if exercise brings on chest pain, and from about 33% to about 11% if exercise does not bring on chest pain.

Other effects: female (rather than male) lowers it; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (rather than fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less) lowers it; a reversible defect on the thallium scan (rather than any other thallium stress test result) lowers it (on the training data only).
Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: atypical angina (rather than any other chest pain type) raises it (on the training data only).

ann_29.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a slightly higher predicted risk of heart disease if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than an upsloping ST segment (about 35%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 33%) (on the training data only).
This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.8 percentage points).
